title: Hazardous Waste Management
overview: It is essential for anyone involved in hazardous waste management, whether in disposal or transportation, to gain the necessary knowledge and skills for safe handling. The first step in effective hazardous waste management is understanding what qualifies as hazardous material and what does not. Proper handling methods are critical to ensure that hazardous materials are managed safely, minimizing the risk of incidents such as fires, explosions, or toxic gas releases from improper containment. This course provides the expertise needed for safe handling practices and developing contingency or emergency plans.
audience: This course is beneficial for professionals working in industries that generate hazardous materials and are responsible for developing contingency or emergency response plans. It is also designed for individuals directly or indirectly involved in cleaning areas contaminated with hazardous waste.
methodology: This interactive course will include group discussions, case studies, syndicate work, and practical exercises, allowing participants to apply their newfound knowledge to real-world hazardous waste management scenarios.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Differentiate between various types of hazardous waste and apply the appropriate pre-transport and disposal methods, leading to cost reductions.
Implement engineering controls to ensure that all personnel involved in hazardous waste management are equipped with the necessary Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
Prevent accidents by applying correct handling methods for drums and containers used in hazardous waste management.
Identify training requirements for those working with hazardous waste.
Develop emergency response plans for the release of hazardous substances.

items.text: Definition and classification of hazardous waste

Safety and health programs for hazardous waste operations
